title: Quick check: AI Product Experimentation

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes hypotheses and experiment design in the context of ai product experimentation?
options: The concept can be implemented entirely in a prompt; application validation and testing are unnecessary.
Use the largest available model for every task and skip a baseline or documented acceptance criteria.

Hypotheses and experiment design supports a repeatable development workflow. Keep dependencies and model choices explicit, preserve small input/output fixtures, isolate credentials from source code, and document how another learner can reproduce the result on a compatible environment.
A fluent result is enough to establish correctness, so the input and assumptions do not need checking.
questions.answer_key: Hypotheses and experiment design supports a repeatable development workflow. Keep dependencies and model choices explicit, preserve small input/output fixtures, isolate credentials from source code, and document how another learner can reproduce the result on a compatible environment.
questions.explanation: Hypotheses and experiment design supports a repeatable development workflow. Keep dependencies and model choices explicit, preserve small input/output fixtures, isolate credentials from source code, and document how another learner can reproduce the result on a compatible environment. This is why the lesson treats the concept as something to apply and verify, not as a guarantee of quality.

questions.prompt: Which practice gives the clearest evidence that comparing model and interface alternatives is working in ai product experimentation?
options: Change the prompt, model, data, and settings at the same time, then attribute any difference to one cause.
Use representative cases, an explicit success criterion, and retained failure examples; compare results against a baseline before relying on the behavior.
Test only one easy input, then assume the behavior generalizes to every language, user, and data source.
Skip validation because a well-formatted answer implies the model followed the intended process.
questions.answer_key: Use representative cases, an explicit success criterion, and retained failure examples; compare results against a baseline before relying on the behavior.
questions.explanation: Comparing model and interface alternatives should be evaluated with evidence appropriate to its use. Representative tests and a baseline help reveal failures and avoid overstating what the example proves.

questions.prompt: A team applies hypotheses and experiment design from ai product experimentation and gets a plausible result, but it has not checked an edge case. What should it do next?
options: Reproduce the case with controlled input, check source/evidence and intermediate steps where available, test an edge case, and document remaining uncertainty.
Accept the result because confidence and fluency are reliable substitutes for measurement.
Remove guardrails or access checks to make the next run more likely to succeed.
Increase model size and deploy immediately, without retaining a baseline or regression tests.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the case with controlled input, check source/evidence and intermediate steps where available, test an edge case, and document remaining uncertainty.
questions.explanation: A plausible answer is not proof. Controlled tests, evidence checks, and explicit uncertainty help identify incorrect assumptions and unsafe failure modes.
